answer: Each agent must lock a refundable bond before it can submit work, and a randomly selected peer can challenge a submission with evidence; if an independent review confirms fraud, the bond is slashed and the challenger is paid. Influence is proportional to bonded value, so splitting one stake among many fake names creates no extra voting power. Whether a task concerns a glacier, island, or dune, an attacker must lock more real capital for more influence—and risks losing it.
